title: Willow Retail — outbound approach & objection crib
content:
Quick sketch of account + outreach plan for Willow (regional retail chain, 120 stores, loyalty program + chat via app). Goal: pilot for conversational returns assistant + FAQ + in-store POS summarization. Keep small (2 stores), show cost/performance uplift (latency < 350ms for app, 70% deflection over contact center).

Account snapshot (public + notes):
- HQ: Portland, OR. Founded 2009. Focus on neighborhood grocers / community loyalty.
- Tech signals: job postings for mobile eng + data infra; uses Snowflake + Segment (job postings + StackShare). Likely cloud-first.
- Current CX: outsourced contact center partner; chat bot is rule-based (Intercom?). Low NPS on returns flow mentioned in Glassdoor reviews.
- Decision makers to target: VP Digital (Alicia Morgan, LinkedIn), Dir of CX Ops (Tomir Patel), Head of Engineering (Leah Huang). Store ops champion: regional ops lead — try to find name in Press/Linkedin.

Why Redwood matters to Willow (short bullets):
- Lower per-token inference cost at scale (demo numbers: 35–50% reduction vs naive hosted + batching).
- Predictable latency and fallback: Dedicated capacity + automatic model fallback keeps app responsive during peak grocery hours.
- Private deploy option for PII (returns receipts) — can satisfy security/legal ask.
- Observable metrics: token-level cost + per-route latency to justify ROI to finance.

Suggested outcomes for a 3-month pilot:
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): data ingest & privacy review — identify returns transcripts + sample FAQs
- Phase 1 (4 weeks): model endpoint + UI integration (mobile chat) — hosted or dedicated depending on SLA
- Phase 2 (4 weeks): measurement & iterate (deflection, latency, CSAT impact)
- Phase 3 (2 weeks): rollout plan for 2 pilot stores -> success criteria: 50% issue deflection, median latency < 350ms, cost <$0.02 per user interaction (TBD)

Outbound sequence (lean, 6 touches):
1) Short email to VP Digital (Alicia): one-liner value + micro-case (other retailer saved $X). CTA: 15-min sync.
2) LinkedIn message to Dir CX Ops (Tomir): attach 1-pg pilot sketch, ask about returns volume.
3) Cold demo offer to Head Eng (Leah): quick perf numbers + invite to run 30-min perf lab using their sample payload.
4) Follow-up email with customer story + ask to intro ops champion.
5) Call / voicemail to Alicia if no reply after 7 days. Keep note: avoid long product decks.
6) If still no reply, outreach to store ops for operational angle (short ask about returns peak hours).

Sample cold email (very short, editable):
Subject: Cut returns contact center volume by 40% — quick pilot?
Hi Alicia — quick note, we helped a 150-store grocer reduce returns contact volume by ~40% with a focused LLM pilot (returns assistant + receipts summarization). Would you be open to 15 minutes next week to see a one-page pilot and latency/cost numbers tailored to Willow?
— Samantha

Anticipated objections + one-liners to test:
- "We don't want PII in the cloud." -> "Understood — we can run a VPC/private deployment with your KMS, or redaction pipeline before tokens leave your network. Legal already signed similar SOC2 addendum for retailer X."
- "LLMs are unpredictable / hallucinate." -> "We build retrieval-augmented responses + structured outputs and regression tests tied to your prompt set; we can run the same evals in staging so you see error modes before go-live."
- "Costs will balloon." -> "Pilot scoped to limited routes and uses batching+caching to show unit economics; we provide per-token and route-level dashboards so finance can see the dollars in real time."
- "We already have a chatbot vendor." -> "Great — we can augment their bot with high-quality LLM responses on the return flows and show measurable deflection without ripping out existing infra."

Meeting prep checklist (for first intro call):
- Ask: weekly returns volume, % of returns requiring human agent, existing SLAs for mobile chat
- Tech: current stack + any compliance constraints (PCI, PII), propensity to install private agents
- Ops: peak hours, busiest store windows, key metrics they track (CSAT, handle time)
- Stakeholders: who signs pilot, who owns data access, legal contacts

Notes to self / tactical follow-ups:
- Find reference retail case study showing cost numbers (ask Diego for customer A data).
- Maya to draft 1-pg pilot sketch with timing and cost ranges by next Wed (2026-02-17).
- Pull returns transcript sample from public reviews (scrape examples) to demo hallucination risk and scoring.
- Create short perf lab template: 5 queries, measure p50/p95, token count, cost estimate.

Open questions / risks (flag in red for internal):
- They outsource contact center — will vendor contract block us from integrating with transcripts? Need legal check.
- Loyalty data might live in a proprietary system; does Willow want LLM to see loyalty IDs? If no, add redaction + linking later.
- Measurement: how do they attribute deflection? Need access to contact center logs or conversation ids.

Quick CRM tags for import:
- account_tier: mid-market
- interest: returns automation, chat
- pilot_size: 2 stores
- next_step: send pilot 1-pg

Rough timeline: aim to get 15-min intro by end of Feb (2026-02-26). If no engagement by mid-March, deprioritize until Q2 operational budget cycle.

Draft follow-up LinkedIn message (Tomir):
Hey Tomir — noticed Willow flagged returns as a CX pain in your Q4 hiring note. We run small, low-risk pilots to reduce contact center load for returns with predictable latency and cost controls — would you be open to a quick 10-min convo? I can share a 1-pg pilot sketch.

Final misc notes (choppy):
- Keep deck <5 slides. Ops cares about numbers not architecture.
- Avoid big-brand vendor comparisons in first outreach.
- If legal balks, propose data escrow + redaction as interim.
- Follow-up cadence: 3x in first 2 weeks, then pause 30d.

---
End of scratch — merge into outreach tracker once Maya finalizes pilot one-pager.
